findings.title: conversation_trajectories: 2 of 5 speakers are invisible in the plot (zero-length duplicated-point strokes) while still getting legend entries; markdown wrongly calls the duplicated row 'a drawable line'
findings.description: Utterances with a single embedding window get their row duplicated so the array has 2 rows, but a line between two identical 3D points has zero length and renders no visible ink. In the tutorial's seeded conversation, speakers 'implode573' and 'mattgrum' each have only single-window utterances (windows=[1]), so their strokes are invisible in both the static figure and the serial animation, yet both appear in the legend. The markdown (cell 7) claims the duplication yields 'a drawable line', and the static-plot caption says 'Each color is one speaker; each stroke is one utterance' -- a reader cannot find those two speakers' strokes. A marker fallback (e.g. plotting single-window utterances with 'o') or a caption caveat would fix it.
findings.repro:
cd /tmp && MPLBACKEND=Agg python - <<'EOF'
import random, re
from convokit import Corpus, download
corpus = Corpus(filename=download('reddit-corpus-small'))
SW=3
usable=lambda c:[u for u in c.get_chronological_utterance_list() if u.text and u.text.strip() and u.text.strip() not in ('[deleted]','[removed]')]
split=lambda t:[s for s in (x.strip() for x in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', t)) if s]
cw=lambda t:(max(1,len(split(t))-SW+1) if len(split(t))>=SW else 1)
def substantial(c):
    u=usable(c)
    if not 10<=len(u)<=40 or len(set(x.speaker.id for x in u))<2: return False
    return sum(1 for x in u if cw(x.text.strip())>=2)/len(u)>=0.6
cand=[c for c in corpus.iter_conversations() if substantial(c)]
random.seed(25); conv=random.choice(cand)
per={}
for u in usable(conv): per.setdefault(u.speaker.id,[]).append(cw(u.text.strip()))
for s,w in per.items(): print(s,w,'ALL-INVISIBLE' if all(x==1 for x in w) else '')
EOF
findings.expected: Every legend entry corresponds to at least one visible stroke, or the text explains that single-window utterances are invisible/point-like.
findings.actual:
speaker 'implode573': windows=[1] -> ALL-INVISIBLE=True
speaker 'mattgrum': windows=[1] -> ALL-INVISIBLE=True
(visual: conv_cell11_out0.png shows no yellow-green or blue strokes despite legend entries)

findings.title: Streaming: stream_max is not honored when smaller than stream_init (consumes and reports stream_init samples)
findings.description: hyp.plot(stream, stream_init=500, stream_max=300) consumes the full 500-sample head and reports stream_info['n_samples']=500, contradicting the docstring ('stop streaming after this many samples'). Root cause: hypertools/io/streaming.py line 207 'head_rows = list(itertools.islice(it, int(stream_init)))' never clamps the head to stream_max. Clamp with min(stream_init, stream_max) or raise a clear error for the inconsistent combination.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
def inf(dim=10, seed=1):
    rng=np.random.default_rng(seed)
    while True: yield rng.standard_normal(dim)
f=hyp.plot(inf(), stream_init=500, stream_chunk=100, stream_max=300, show=False)
print(f.stream_info['n_samples'])  # 500, not <=300
EOF
findings.expected: At most 300 samples consumed/reported (or a ValueError explaining stream_max < stream_init).

findings.title: Streaming: one sample beyond stream_max is silently consumed from the underlying stream by the truncation peek
findings.description: With stream_init=200, stream_chunk=100, stream_max=1200 the instrumented generator was pulled 1201 times: hypertools/io/streaming.py line 278 'truncated = any(True for _ in itertools.islice(it, 1))' peeks one extra sample to set stream_info['truncated'] and discards it. For stateful or costly streams (hardware acquisition, paid API pages, LSL) that sample is silently lost, and neither the plot() docstring nor the tutorial mentions it. Document the peek or use a non-consuming sentinel where possible.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
pulls=[0]
def gen():
    rng=np.random.default_rng(0)
    while True:
        pulls[0]+=1
        yield rng.standard_normal(10)
hyp.plot(gen(), stream_init=200, stream_chunk=100, stream_max=1200, show=False)
print('pulled:', pulls[0])  # 1201
EOF
findings.expected: Exactly stream_max samples consumed, or the +1 peek documented in the stream_max docstring.

findings.title: predict error-type/message polish: fitted-model reuse mismatch leaks sklearn internals; AutoRegressor short-train check raises AssertionError
findings.description: (1) Reusing a fitted AutoRegressor (the stock tutorial's return_model=True workflow) on data with a different column count fails with sklearn's 'X has 10 features, but Ridge is expecting 30 features as input.' -- nothing names predict_new, the fitted forecaster, or the column mismatch with the fitting data. (2) hyp.predict(3-row df, model='AutoRegressor') raises AssertionError ('AutoRegressor needs more than lags=10 observations to fit; got 3') -- helpful text, wrong exception type for user-facing validation (assertions vanish under python -O), inconsistent with the ValueErrors used elsewhere (e.g. 't must be >= 1').
findings.expected: Hypertools-branded ValueError naming the fitted forecaster's expected columns; ValueError (not AssertionError) for the short-train case.
findings.actual:
RAISED ValueError: X has 10 features, but Ridge is expecting 30 features as input.
RAISED AssertionError: AutoRegressor needs more than lags=10 observations to fit; got 3

findings.title: impute silently fills never-observed (all-NaN) columns with 0.0 without any warning
findings.description: hyp.impute on a frame whose column has zero observations (a dead sensor) returns 0.0 for the whole column, for both Kalman and PPCA, with no warning. PPCA already warns helpfully about fully-missing ROWS (naming the Kalman fix, GH #169); a matching warning for fully-missing COLUMNS would prevent scientists from mistaking fabricated zeros for data. (Also applies to an entirely all-NaN frame, which imputes without complaint.)
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((50, 3)), columns=list('abc'))
df['c'] = np.nan
out = hyp.impute(df, model='Kalman')
print(out['c'].abs().max())  # 0.0, no warning emitted
EOF
findings.expected: UserWarning: column 'c' has no observed values; imputed values are uninformed (filled with 0.0).
findings.actual: Column returned as all 0.0 with no warning (both model='Kalman' and model='PPCA').

findings.title: Notebook metadata hygiene: streaming_data.ipynb has no kernelspec; conversation_trajectories and streaming_data each have a cell missing the nbformat-4.5 id
findings.description: streaming_data.ipynb's metadata lacks a kernelspec (the other three tutorials declare python3), so fresh Jupyter/Colab sessions prompt for a kernel on open/Run-All. Additionally the first (pip-install) cell of conversation_trajectories.ipynb and streaming_data.ipynb lacks the 'id' field required by nbformat 4.5: every programmatic read emits 'MissingIDFieldWarning: Cell is missing an id field, this will become a hard error in future nbformat versions'. Normalizing the notebooks (nbformat.validator.normalize or jupyter nbconvert --to notebook) fixes both.
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import json
for n in ['conversation_trajectories','projectile_kalman','stock_forecasting','streaming_data']:
    raw = json.load(open(f'/Users/jmanning/hypertools/docs/tutorials/{n}.ipynb'))
    ks = raw.get('metadata', {}).get('kernelspec')
    noid = sum(1 for c in raw['cells'] if 'id' not in c)
    print(n, 'kernelspec=', 'MISSING' if ks is None else ks.get('name'), 'cells_missing_id=', noid)
EOF
findings.expected: All four tutorials declare a python3 kernelspec and every cell has an id (nbformat 4.5).
findings.actual:
conversation_trajectories kernelspec= python3 cells_missing_id= 1
projectile_kalman kernelspec= python3 cells_missing_id= 0
stock_forecasting kernelspec= python3 cells_missing_id= 0
streaming_data kernelspec= MISSING cells_missing_id= 1

findings.title: predict/impute model-name matching is case-sensitive ('kalman' rejected)
findings.description: hyp.predict(x, model='kalman') raises 'unknown predict model' even though the message immediately lists 'Kalman'. The dispatcher already special-cases an alias table ('GP' -> 'GaussianProcess'), so a case-insensitive fallback would be cheap and matches how users type model names; same applies to hyp.impute ('ppca' vs 'PPCA'). The current error message is excellent, so this is polish rather than a defect.
findings.repro: python -c "import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.predict(pd.DataFrame({'a': np.arange(30.)}), model='kalman', t=2)"
findings.expected: 'kalman' resolves to Kalman (case-insensitive lookup), or the docs state that names are case-sensitive.
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown predict model 'kalman'; supported names: Kalman, GaussianProcess, AutoRegressor, ARIMA, Laplace, Chronos (or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, a Forecaster subclass, or a Forecaster instance directly)
